post.description:
Always 204, whatever the address and whatever SMTP is doing: the email
is queued (never sent inline), so the answer, its timing and a mail
outage reveal nothing about which emails have accounts (P1-7).

Change the password and sign out every other device. The caller keeps
working on a re-issued session: its old one died with the epoch bump.

get.description: Label map for the signed-in tenant's industry.
Public preview used during signup/onboarding (before a session exists).

schema.title: Response List Users Team Users Get

post.description:
204 once the invite is recorded. The email is queued in the same
transaction and sent after commit, so a mail outage can't fail it.

schema.title: Response List Roles Team Roles Get
Response List Pipelines Crm Pipelines Get

post.description:
Bulk-load leads from a CSV posted as the raw request body.

Row-level tolerance on purpose: a 2,000-row file with three bad rows imports
1,997 and names the three — failing the whole file sends the user back to
Excel to hunt for a needle. Duplicate checks run inside the same transaction,
so a phone number appearing twice *within the file* is caught too.

get.description: Their data is theirs — export is also what makes import trustworthy.

schema.title: Response List Leads Crm Leads Get

post.description:
Answers across every module the tenant has enabled.

Deliberately not gated on a single section: the whole point is that one
question can span sales, stock and staff. Access is scoped by passing the
enabled sections down to the guard, which allowlists views accordingly — so
a POS-only tenant can never reach a CRM view.

schema.title: Response List Invoices Crm Invoices Get

get.description:
One page of the catalog; `X-Total-Count` is how many match in all.

Archived products stay listable behind a flag — otherwise archiving is a
one-way trip and the catalog can never be un-done. The default page size
(50 for a search, 200 otherwise) is what the till and pickers have always
received; the Products page pages with limit/offset so nothing past the
first page is unreachable. Ties on name are broken by id so pages never
overlap or skip a row.

schema.title: Response List Products Pos Products Get

post.description:
Price a cart exactly as a sale would be priced, without recording it, so
the till shows the server's own total (tax-exclusive prices included).

schema.title: Response List Suppliers Pos Suppliers Get

post.description:
Created straight into 'ordered' — the SME phones the order in; this
record exists so the delivery can be received against it.

schema.title: Response List Pos Pos Purchase Orders Get

post.description:
Goods arrive. Stock rises here and nowhere else on the inbound side.

Partial deliveries are the norm, so lines carry received_qty and the PO only
flips to 'received' once every line is complete. Over-receiving is refused —
a delivery larger than the order is a paperwork problem to resolve, not a
number to absorb silently.

schema.title: Response Current Drawer Pos Drawer Current Get

post.description:
Freezes the expected figure at close: the shift's reconciliation is
evidence, and a later sale edit must not silently rewrite a signed-off
variance.

schema.title: Response Drawer History Pos Drawer History Get

post.description:
Bulk-load the catalog from CSV. A shop's stock list almost always already
exists in Excel — retyping 500 SKUs by hand is how trials die.

get.description:
Velocity-based reorder advice: flag products running out relative to how
fast they sell (30-day velocity), plus anything below its low-stock line.

60-day look-ahead: upcoming occasions with projected demand per product
from recent velocity × event duration × expected uplift.
Submission log — the retailer's evidence of what was filed and what was not.

schema.title: Response List Invoices Fbr Invoices Get

post.description:
Settle a filing whose outcome is unknown (the connection dropped after
it was sent). FBR offers no lookup, so a person checks IRIS: filed (record
FBR's number, never resend) or not filed (send it once more).

schema.title: Response List Employees Hrms Employees Get

post.description:
Give an employee their own self-service login. Sends an invite they accept
to set a password — the same flow as team invites, on the Employee role.

schema.title: Response List Attendance Hrms Attendance Get

get.description:
Last 7 days as a matrix: one derived status per employee per day.

Derivation mirrors the payroll rules exactly — the matrix and the payslip
must never disagree about the same day. In particular: today with no
check-in is 'pending', not absent (the day isn't over), and WFH is its own
state, never leave.

schema.title: Response List Shifts Hrms Shifts Get

post.description:
Put an employee on a shift from `date_from`. An open-ended assignment
that started earlier is closed the day before; any other overlap is a 409,
so a day never has two shifts. It applies to punches from then on — days
already derived keep their derivation.

schema.title: Response List Shift Assignments Hrms Shift Assignments Get
Response List Leave Hrms Leave Get
Response Leave Balances Hrms Leave Balances Get

post.description:
Approval needs hrms:admin — with plain write, anyone who could request
leave could approve their own (the audit's separation-of-duties finding).

schema.title: Response List Holidays Hrms Holidays Get

get.description:
Monthly payslips: gross − absence deduction − FBR tax. `month` = YYYY-MM.
Everyone's pay is on it, so it needs a payroll key, not hrms:read (D-42).

schema.title: Response My Attendance Me Attendance Get
Response My Leave Me Leave Get

post.description:
An employee requests their own leave. The employee_id in the body is
ignored — it is forced to the caller, so nobody can file against someone
else. Approval still belongs to an admin (hrms:admin).

schema.title: Response My Balances Me Leave Balances Get
Response My Payslips Me Payslips Get
Response List Plans Billing Plans Get

post.description:
Customer states they have sent the bank transfer.

This records the claim and nothing more. It deliberately does NOT activate
the plan: the payer is not the party who gets to confirm that money arrived.
A human reconciles the transfer against the reference and runs
`scripts/activate_payment.py`, which is the only path to an active plan.

get.description:
One page; `X-Total-Count` is how many match. A phone typed in any
format matches its E.164 key.

post.description:
With contacts.contact.create: any field, and a 409 naming the likely
duplicates. From the till (pos.sale.create only): name, phone and email,
and a duplicate answer that names no one — matched on phone alone and
reported as a count — so adding a customer can't be used to read the
contact book. The cashier then finds them with lookup by phone.

get.description:
Exact E.164 lookup for the till (and the WhatsApp inbox later). Every
live holder comes back: a shared number is the cashier's pick, never an
automatic match.

post.description: Merge up to four contacts into one, in one transaction (soft merge).

Side by side: the records, the fields that differ, and how many
records would move from each (sales only for those who can read POS).

get.description: Open items, each with the contacts holding the clashing key.

schema.title: Response Review Queue Contacts Review Get

get.description:
Contact 360: the record, its company or people, addresses, and what
the other modules hold for it.

delete.description: Archive, never delete: sales, invoices and old receipts keep pointing here.

get.description:
Other contacts holding this one's phone, email or NTN (archived ones
too); keys shared by more than the threshold are listed, not matched.

Everything that happened to this contact or to a record rolled up to
it, newest first, limited to the record types the caller may read
(TIMELINE_ENTITY_KEYS). Contacts merged into this one bring their
history: the timeline is append-only, so reads follow merged_into_id
instead of rewriting old events (contact_merge registry, "follow").

schema.title: Response Contact Timeline Contacts  Contact Id  Timeline Get
Response Add Note Contacts  Contact Id  Notes Post

get.description: The contact a lead is qualified to, or null.

schema.title: Response Lead Contact Crm Leads  Lead Id  Contact Get

post.description:
Link the lead to a contact, or create the contact from the lead. A
create that finds a contact with the same phone or email answers 409
with them, so the user links instead of duplicating (unless `force`).
Create contacts for this tenant's leads (option b). Safe to rerun.
Leave the lead without a contact; the backfill won't queue it again.

FbrResolve.title: FbrResolve
FbrResolve.description: An owner's answer for a filing in `unknown`, after checking IRIS.

LocaleOut.title: LocaleOut
LocaleOut.description: How to render for this caller (12-trd §5.2 `locale`).

QualifyRequest.title: QualifyRequest
QualifyRequest.description: Link the lead to an existing contact, or create one from the lead.

RefundableLine.title: RefundableLine
RefundableLine.description:
A returnable line plus the two figures a refund is computed from
(pricing.refund_for), so the Returns screen previews what will actually be
paid out rather than list price x qty (audit I8).

StageSlice.title: StageSlice
StageSlice.description:
One pipeline stage's standing total. Value and count both, because a stage
holding one large deal and a stage holding twenty small ones are different
situations and a single number hides which you're in.
